content: While taking this medication, it may be necessary to undergo laboratory tests, such as kidney and liver function tests or complete blood counts, to monitor your health. Ensure that you attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose of this medication, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to make up for the missed one. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Avoid flushing medications down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Dispose of this product properly when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last updated in May 2024. It is important to note that this document provides a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this medication and your individual health needs. Before taking amoxicillin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to penicillin, or to cephalosporin antibiotics, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Amoxicillin may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. Amoxicillin can pass into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter the way your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not list all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as some diabetic urine tests, potentially causing false results. In the event of an overdose, if the individual has serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it for other conditions unless directed by your doctor. Prolonged treatment may require additional laboratory and/or medical tests to monitor your health. Always keep all medical and laboratory appointments.
